title: Speed Round: True or Rubbish?
desc: Ten rapid-fire food claims — call true or rubbish on each

questions.q: True or rubbish: Carrots improve your night vision
questions.a: Rubbish — WWII British propaganda to hide the invention of radar. Vitamin A helps general eye health, but won't give you night vision

questions.q: True or rubbish: Twinkies last forever
questions.a: Rubbish — they last about 45 days. The myth comes from their lack of dairy, but they do go stale

questions.q: True or rubbish: Goldfish crackers contain real cheese
questions.a: True — cheddar cheese is listed as an ingredient in the original flavour

questions.q: True or rubbish: Coffee is a fruit
questions.a: True — coffee beans are the seeds of a cherry-like fruit called a coffee cherry

questions.q: True or rubbish: Lobster used to be prison food
questions.a: True — in colonial America, lobster was so abundant it was considered poverty food and fed to servants and prisoners

questions.q: True or rubbish: Nutmeg can be hallucinogenic in large doses
questions.a: True — myristicin in nutmeg can cause hallucinations, but the amount needed also causes severe nausea, so nobody enjoys the experience

questions.q: True or rubbish: A coconut is a nut
questions.a: Rubbish — it's a drupe (a fruit with a fleshy outer layer and a hard shell containing a seed). Same category as peaches and plums

questions.q: True or rubbish: The hole in a pasta spoon measures one serving of spaghetti
questions.a: True — most pasta spoon holes are designed to hold roughly one portion of dry spaghetti

questions.q: True or rubbish: Chocolate was once used as currency
questions.a: True — the Aztecs used cacao beans as money. You could buy a turkey for about 100 beans

questions.q: True or rubbish: Bananas are radioactive enough to set off airport security
questions.a: Rubbish — they contain potassium-40 but the amount is far too tiny to trigger any detector
